💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyundai pulled back the cover on the new 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class.
  • The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand.
  • It has been revealed that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai pulled back the cover on the new 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

It has been revealed that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

An updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a new Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Sharing the stage in LA, the fresh nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

In a recent development, inside, a new cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

Industry observers note that pleos Connect, Hyundai’s upcoming Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

The Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai states the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

According to recent reports, “Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” noted Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the new Elantra is anything but bland.

Recent findings suggest that the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent fresh SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

Recent findings suggest that the sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai states the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

Hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

Sources indicate that editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid prepares, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Massive Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

According to recent reports, if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The company already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

According to recent reports, gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro initiative, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

Recent findings suggest that at launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Sources indicate that also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

According to recent reports, the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US customers can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The new landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

Recent findings suggest that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

“You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release noted. Google’s upcoming Memory summary feature for Gemini lets consumers view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

The Last Time the Fed Kept Raising Rates, the S&P 500 Fell 25%. History States Long-Term Investors Still Came Out Ahead.

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure is the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index.
  • Industry observers note that this has forced the central bank's hand, as it's an institution tasked with controlling rising prices across the economy.
  • In a recent development, stock market investors aren't exactly encouraged by this trend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 23, 2026 at 4:18PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure is the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index. A 2% reading is the long-run target. Even excluding food and energy, the U.S. has been running well above that for five years.

Industry observers note that this has forced the central bank's hand, as it's an institution tasked with controlling rising prices across the economy. It raised the fed funds rate 25 basis points in September. The market is certain another hike is in store next month. The big banks believe the benchmark rate will continue to rise in early 2027.

In a recent development, stock market investors aren't exactly encouraged by this trend. The last time the Fed kept raising rates, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC +4.73%) fell 25%. You might hesitate to put money to work right now.

According to recent reports, it's better to be bullish, though. History indicates long-term investors still come out ahead.

Recent findings suggest that in March 2022, the Fed rolled out its previous tightening campaign. From February 2022 to August 2023, it lifted the upper end of its target range from 0.25% to 5.50%.

Inflation forced the move. The PCE price index climbed 6.8% year over year in June 2022, its fastest pace since 1982. The central bank had held rates near zero for almost two years following the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. It had to play catch-up.

In a recent development, higher rates can squeeze stocks in multiple ways. They raise borrowing costs for companies, which can pressure capital investments. And they make bonds and cash look more attractive by comparison, weighing on valuations.

It has been revealed that wall Street didn't take it well. From its January 2022 high to its October 2022 low, the S&P 500 index shed 25%. The last bear market saw roughly a quarter of the market's value vanish in about nine months.

Many investors might have missed this detail. Stocks bottomed even as the Fed still had months of rate hikes ahead. Its final increase didn't come until July 2023. The market, a forward-looking machine, started climbing long before borrowing costs stopped rising.

Recent findings suggest that betting on the recovery still demanded patience from investors. The benchmark didn't close above its January 2022 high until Jan. 19, 2024. It took two years just to get back to even.

The momentum didn't let up. The S&P 500 at the moment sits 50% above its 2022 peak (as of Nov. 19), even though it's 8% below its record. That's also after the Fed resumed hiking in September and with the latest meeting minutes showing that almost all officials expect additional increases.

It has been revealed that run the numbers. If you invested $10,000 in the S&P 500 at its January 2022 high, you watched it shrink to about $7,500 by that October. If you had steady hands, it would be worth roughly $15,000 today, before dividends.

In a recent development, the investor who sold near the bottom locked in a $2,500 loss, which would have relieved the pain. A second, harder decision was next. You had to figure out when to get back in. It's easier remarked than done. And few people buy confidently while panic-filled headlines are widespread.

Industry observers note that that's the trap of market timing. You have to be right twice. Selling at the start of a hiking cycle feels prudent to cut losses. But the last cycle highlighted it was a costly mistake.

Meanwhile, anyone who kept investing through the slump was fine. From its October 2022 low, the index has roughly doubled.

None of this guarantees a repeat performance. Today's inflation is tied partly to an energy shock, and rates could climb further than markets expect. There's no rule saying stocks can't fall hard again. Investors need to accept that possibility.

According to recent reports, A 25% drawdown definitely hurts, even when history proves it's temporary. But having a five-year-plus horizon changes the math. The goal is to stay invested long enough for corporate earnings growth, the key fundamental tailwind, to do the heavy lifting. The goal isn't to predict the Fed's next move. Nobody does that consistently.

Rate hikes are back, and the playbook hasn't changed. Time in the market beats timing the market.

But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

A new feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

It has been revealed that with a new feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

Industry observers note that the new app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone users. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

Genesis Launches Hybrids at the LA Auto Show, EREV Coming in 2027

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Korean luxury automaker Genesis introduced its first hybrid models this week, debuting newly introduced powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show.
  • Industry observers note that the hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies.
  • The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Korean luxury automaker Genesis introduced its first hybrid models this week, debuting newly introduced powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show. The tech giant claims the electrified system is both more efficient and more powerful than the current nonhybrid versions. For buyers who want a more battery-focused experience, Genesis teased an upcoming 640-mile extended-range electric vehicle due to arrive in early 2027.

Industry observers note that the hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies. Hybrids, in particular, have attracted attention because they behave like traditional combustion cars: There’s no need to install home charging hardware or change familiar driving and refueling habits. Just get in and reap better fuel economy with every mile.

The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain. Genesis says the system is 16% more powerful than the gasoline-only version, outputting 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque. A new liquid-cooled battery pack improves thermal management and allows higher maximum discharge than Hyundai Motor Group’s previous air-cooled hybrid batteries, boosting performance. Both models use a seven-speed automatic transmission adapted to work with the electric motor’s regenerative braking.

Genesis hasn’t declared official fuel economy estimates, but says the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than the standard model, while the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient. Based on current EPA figures, my math puts them in the ballpark of 30 mpg and 27 mpg, respectively. Any improvement is good, but those aren’t exactly earth-shattering gains. We’ll have to wait for the official ratings to be sure.

Each hybrid can be toggled into a silent EV mode for short distances — good for gliding into a driveway, garage or parking deck without waking the neighbors. However, without a plug, all the energy in the battery ultimately comes from the gas tank.

A new Stay Mode lets owners run the climate control and infotainment without starting the engine for around 30 minutes. I like to think of it as the “moment of zen in the driveway before you have to go inside and face responsibility” mode, or maybe the “eating lunch in your car” mode. It’s similar to Toyota’s My Room Mode on its hybrids.

It has been revealed that aside from the powertrain, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their combustion counterparts. Hybrid-specific touches include a three-dimensional G-Matrix grille inlay redesigned for these models, as well as latest exterior colors.

It has been revealed that inside, a 27-inch OLED display combining the instrument cluster and navigation stretches halfway across the dashboard. Tech features include Digital Key 2 Premium, which lets owners use their phone instead of a key fob to unlock and start the car, and active road noise cancellation. Genesis’ driver-assistance suite is headlined by the Highway Drive Assist 2 steering assistance system and the Remote Smart Parking Assist 2, which enables automatic parking with the driver inside or just nearby the car.

Prices for the sedan and SUV haven’t been unveiled. Final specifications and EPA fuel economy figures are expected closer to the early 2027 launch window.

My cynical side says that these new models are just Genesis doing what Toyota has done since the RX 400h debuted in 2004. (To be fair, Genesis didn’t become an independent brand until 2015, so its rival has a bit of a head start.) In practical terms, the move brings Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand into parity with other group members and luxury car competitors that have rolled out updated hybrids over the last year, and meets customers’ increasing demand for more energy-efficient cars where they are.

In addition to its first hybrid sedan and SUV, Genesis executives announced that the brand will expand the availability of its wild-styled, high-performance GV60 Magma full-electric SUV to more states and markets to meet higher-than-expected demand.

Industry observers note that at the debut event in LA, the brand also teased an upcoming extended-range EV — an EV with an onboard gasoline generator, essentially a very advanced plug-in hybrid — set to launch in early 2027. The EREV model is targeting over 640 miles before its “all-latest high-performance battery” and gas tank both run dry, but Genesis didn’t give further details about the upcoming model.

Editor’s note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Tech Report: Google Wallet comes to your iPhone – but without this feature

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (481 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone people in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • It has been revealed that the latest Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone people in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the newly introduced Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

It has been revealed that the latest Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app customers on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

According to recent reports, agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

It has been revealed that the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

It has been revealed that along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google revealed AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

#97158. Andrew Garfield on Becoming Sam Altman in ‘Artificial’: ‘I’m Dying to Understand This Person’

Andrew Garfield on Becoming Sam Altman in ‘Artificial’: ‘I’m Dying to Understand This Person’

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1234 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.
  • Industry observers note that rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec.
  • Sources indicate that garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.

Industry observers note that rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec. 25 release. The biopic follows the rise of OpenAI, focusing on Altman’s relationships — particularly with his cofounder Ilya Sutskever (Yura Borisov) — as he relentlessly pursues success amid Silicon Valley’s artificial intelligence power struggle.

Sources indicate that garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set. His mission as an actor is to get to the “central truths” of who a person is, he said, “and try to merge my soul with theirs. And like all of us, Sam has so many facets.”.

In a recent development, that includes physical traits. Garfield says he had to lose weight and change his gait and voice to try to match Altman’s. The semblance is striking. From his bouncy stride to his clipped, gravelly speech, Garfield effortlessly emulates the Altman we’ve seen in interviews and Congressional testimonies. It’s a remarkable transformation — down to the sly, coaxing glint in his eyes — showcasing the breadth of Garfield’s acting talent.

But it goes beyond physicality. Garfield had to dig deep internally to find elements “that felt like they were a match” with Altman, he stated. The result is an astonishingly believable portrayal of a multidimensional figure, at once pensive and inscrutable.

“There is a responsibility,” Garfield told me. “I take it very, very seriously to play any character, but particularly someone who’s alive, someone who’s pretty much my age. But also, maybe the greater responsibility is making sure that we interrogate these human beings that are leading our world into the next chapter, it seems.”.

“And it feels like our job as storytellers to reflect the times we’re in,” he added, “and no better way of doing that than by looking at the human beings — their personal relationships, their souls, all the diamond facets of their souls — and interrogate the people that have the power over our culture right now.”.

Industry observers note that artificial explores OpenAI’s rise through a rather bleak lens, with questions of moral responsibility and safety looming over the protagonists as they navigate the company’s success. The film is laced with dark satire, which offers moments of levity amid otherwise weighty meditations on the technology’s long-term impact.

In one scene, when Sutskever is asked about the difference between AI and artificial general intelligence, which can theoretically match or even surpass human ability, he plainly responds, “It’s like how rocket ships are different from scooters.” He goes on to tell his cohorts that this is achievable “in your lifetime — well, maybe not yours or yours or yours,” as he points to the less youthful figures in the room. Moments like these elicited generous laughter from the audience.

According to recent reports, director Luca Guadagnino, known for deeply character-driven stories, such as Challengers and Call Me by Your Name, mentioned he was following the news about Sam Altman’s temporary ousting from OpenAI in 2023 and was fascinated by the “Shakespearean feud” leading to that moment. Guadagnino applies his signature character-centric approach to OpenAI’s story, relying on slow, measured beats, piercing close-ups and suspenseful music to relay the stakes of each pivotal moment.

“It’s never about the object; it’s always about the people,” Guadagnino said during a panel discussion after the screening. “It’s not about AGI or AI. It’s about the conflict between worldview and way of being, embodied by people that clash or fight for the vision they have.”.

He also said, “The point for me was more about trying to understand: How did the possibility of an incredible technology that can help all of us turn into the opportunity to get power in your hands and to become self-entitled?”.

According to recent reports, garfield is no stranger to portraying prominent figures in the tech world, having played Eduardo Saverin, Facebook’s co-founder and former chief financial officer, in 2010’s The Social Network. On the surface, Artificial seems like a spiritual successor, recounting another defining moment in the tech industry. But the films differ in both tone and approach, with Artificial trading rapid-fire drama for a darker, more existential theme that occasionally ventures into more technical territory. What the films do share is a focus on bold, forceful personalities.

“From that experience, I suppose, I was very curious about what it takes to win in this particular late-stage capitalist world that we’re in with these emerging technologies,” Garfield remarked during the panel discussion. “What does it take to hold Sauron’s Ring of Power and not be completely burnt up by it? Is it possible to not completely lose yourself to that overwhelming, exponentially growing possibility and power?”.

According to recent reports, comic relief also arrives in the form of Ike Barinholtz playing OpenAI cofounder and tech mogul Elon Musk. By portraying him as a brutish, aloof figure who saunters in and out of rooms on a whim, he effectively underscores the absurdity of perceived importance and status. Almost every on-screen moment generated a murmur of laughter in the audience.

In a recent development, “I think we’re all fascinated by these cultural, iconic figures who are leading us into this next stage of culture and society,” Garfield told the crowd. “They’re kind of kids. They’re kind of slightly stuck in an early developmental place, and that felt like a really notable part of Luca’s telling of this story.”.

In a recent development, in fact, he added, “[Guadagnino] would say to us, ‘This is a John Hughes movie. This is a high school, screwball comedy, just with slightly higher stakes — mixed in with a little bit of Invasion of the Body Snatchers.’ A very important part of this is that these are all kind of adolescent, high-school-minded people.”.

Even the way Garfield portrays Altman flippantly perching on couches and sitting cross-legged on tabletops while donning sunglasses — including during serious conversations about the future of OpenAI — was deeply researched.

“We had amazing consultants and researchers that work with us that gave us lots of information that’s not quite in the public arena about our characters,” Garfield remarked. “And Sam is someone who apparently would always sit like he was crisscross applesauce at play school, nursery school [or] kindergarten.”.

In a recent development, ultimately, Artificial poses an open question about where society is headed and whether those at the helm are equipped to lead the charge. Amid weighty explorations of AI’s ramifications, the film paints a haunting, revelatory portrait of the cunning, mercurial figures making decisions that shape our world.

For Garfield, this presented an opportunity to dive deep into a figure like Altman, who, despite his prominence, remains largely elusive in the public eye.

“I just wanted to tell this story and actually uncover for myself, excavate for myself, who is this person?” Garfield told me. “I’m dying to understand this person, and I get to try to understand this person, maybe more than anyone else has ever really tried to. And it feels like a gift to me.”.

#97156. 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1068 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • Fresh data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

Fresh data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

According to recent reports, employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

It has been revealed that the report highlights how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson remarked.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson stated Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he stated.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ upcoming top stressor.

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson remarked. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Recent findings suggest that samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

Industry observers note that “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most key decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

Industry observers note that “When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson noted. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 23, 2026 at 4:18PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) shares closed at $165.05 on Monday, surging 31% from Friday's $125.53, after the tech giant said its board had reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director. The gain added about $950 billion to Nvidia's market value, which rose to about $3.98 trillion.

The rally recovered most of the losses the stock incurred after Huang stepped down. Nvidia disclosed on Nov. 12 that the board had accepted his resignation the day before and named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. The stock closed at $173.73 on Nov. 11 and fell 28% over the next seven trading days. Monday's close is still 5% below that level and 31% below the all-time closing high of $239.24 set on Oct. 6.

Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

Sources indicate that the board voted unanimously on Nov. 22 to bring Huang back, Nvidia announced the following morning. It noted it was "satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead Nvidia" after a series of meetings with him.

The board also mentioned it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and, based on that input, is confident Huang's return "poses no national security risk." Harvey Jones, who became chair when Huang resigned, stays in that role, and Kress stays on as CFO.

"I can't wait to get back to work," Huang said in the release.

Industry observers note that several analysts raised their views within hours. Oppenheimer upgraded the stock to outperform with a $250 price target, calling Huang's return "a win for AI and a win for investors." StoneX upgraded it to buy with a $270 target. Citi raised its target to $240 from $225 and said the move removes the "key overhang" from the CEO change. BMO Capital kept its outperform rating and $240 target.

It has been revealed that bernstein also upgraded the stock to outperform. It had downgraded Nvidia 11 days earlier and cut its price target in half when Huang's exit looked likely.

The same press release that lauds Huang's return lists the remaining open problems. In light of reporting that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," a committee of independent directors is investigating with outside counsel, and the board said that investigation "will proceed to conclusion." Huang said he supports it.

Nvidia also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors, is searching for its first chief compliance officer, and mentioned it "will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.".

According to recent reports, some analysts flagged those problems on Monday. Bernstein kept its $200 target even after the upgrade, saying "this whole mess has brought up some legitimate questions" and will leave some overhangs in place. Goldman Sachs, which rates the stock a buy, stated Nvidia's operations in certain jurisdictions could face more scrutiny. It also questioned whether Nvidia will keep striking large investment deals with partners at the same scale. Baird, which rates the stock neutral with a $200 target, called the combination of Huang's return and strict limits on AI chip access a worst-case scenario for China and said medium-term revenue uncertainty remains.

Only two of those price targets, StoneX's $270 and Oppenheimer's $250, sit above the stock's all-time closing high. Bernstein's and Baird's $200 targets are about 21% above Monday's close.

Monday removed perhaps the biggest single risk for Nvidia (the need to operate without the founder who built it), but it didn't settle the question of why he left. The internal investigation, the government inquiries, and the new compliance structure could still change how Nvidia does business, especially in China.

So is Nvidia a buy? For long-term investors who can live with big swings, yes, but in measured amounts. The stock still trades 31% below its October level with its founder back in charge, and every price target cited here, from $200 to $270, sits above Monday's close. Buyers should expect more volatility until the investigation's findings are known, which matters for semiconductor stocks and AI stocks more broadly, too. Anyone who needs certainty about the inquiries can wait for those results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

The thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

It has been revealed that it could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Industry observers note that unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

The reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this newly introduced platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

It has been revealed that the Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Industry observers note that keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also notes on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Draymond Green rarely, if ever, refuses an opportunity to jab back at his critics.

Following the Golden State Warriors' 88-87 win over the Boston Celtics on Sunday, the veteran forward had plenty to say to those who believe he's not carrying enough of the scoring burden with Stephen Curry sidelined due to an abdominal tear.

Green scored 9 points in the Warriors' win, his highest total of the season thus far. But scoring more has never been his role and he doesn't intend to change that, even with the team's top scorer out.

"I'm never going to, in Year 15, be like 'Oh, man, Steph's out — it's my chance,'" Green told reporters, via The Athletic's Jason Jones. "When I was in Year 6, it was my chance, and I would do what I do.

"But Year 15? That would never be my mindset," he added. "As someone who can do a multitude of things on the basketball court, I would never deduce myself down to you gotta go score.".

Sources indicate that all nine of Green's points on Sunday came in the first quarter when he hit three 3-pointers. Green said after the game that Warriors coach Steve Kerr told him to look to shoot from the corner. That helped Golden State run out to a 27-22 lead after the opening 12 minutes of play.

The Celtics went ahead with a third-quarter surge, leading by 11 at one point. But the Warriors tightened up on defense, allowing them to chip away at the second-half deficit. Golden State finally took an 88-86 lead with 2:38 remaining in regulation on a 3-pointer from Brandin Podziemski.

It has been revealed that on Boston's final possession, Green prevented Jayson Tatum from driving to the basket and forced him to take a fadeaway jumper. But the 16-footer missed and the Warriors got their ninth win of the season.

Industry observers note that tatum was held to 4 points in the second half with Green defending him. That's exactly what Golden State needs Green to do, according to Kerr. Green offered to come off the bench if it would help the team, but Kerr stated his defense is too valuable throughout the game.

According to recent reports, "I told him I had no desire to bring him on the bench because we've got to dig this thing out with defense," Kerr noted, via The Athletic. "And he remains one of the great defenders in the league. He indicated that tonight.".

In a recent development, green is averaging 3.6 points in 14 games this season. If that continues, it would be his lowest scoring average since his rookie campaign in 2012-13. He's also grabbing 4.8 rebounds and dishing out 6.3 assists while shooting 33% on 21 3-point attempts.

Latest Update: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO With the US Government’s Blessing

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia confirmed on Monday that ousted cofounder Jensen Huang would return to his role as CEO after he resigned earlier this month when multiple extramarital affairs became public, including one with a woman that the US intelligence community believes is a Chinese intelligence asset.
  • “The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” remarked Harvey C.
  • According to recent reports, the stunning news comes after weeks of reporting on alleged malfeasance in Huang’s personal and professional lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia confirmed on Monday that ousted cofounder Jensen Huang would return to his role as CEO after he resigned earlier this month when multiple extramarital affairs became public, including one with a woman that the US intelligence community believes is a Chinese intelligence asset.

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” remarked Harvey C. Jones, chair of Nvidia’s board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the tech giant.”.

According to recent reports, the stunning news comes after weeks of reporting on alleged malfeasance in Huang’s personal and professional lives. The scandal broke when The New York Times reported that Huang had a close, personal relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Then came news of a second extramarital affair, leading to Huang’s eventual resignation.

According to recent reports, previously, the board denied it would bring Huang back, despite Huang saying he would return if the board allowed it. Many names were floated as a possible replacement for Huang, including Arm CEO Rene Haas. But many tech experts stated it was difficult to imagine Nvidia without Huang. Apparently, the board agreed.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress temporarily took over as interim CEO, telling investors at its recent earnings call that everything is “business as usual.” But additional reporting revealed that Huang regularly “humiliated” his direct reports, raising serious questions about his management style and the corporate culture of Nvidia, which Huang helped shape more than any other person over the past 20 years.

Nvidia’s stock price rose dramatically on Monday morning with the news of Huang’s return, dragging with it other chipmakers like AMD and Qualcomm and market indices including the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow, which all jumped up on Monday. It’s another sign that Nvidia, as a key firm in the AI industry, is a driving force behind the US and global economy.

Industry observers note that the board added that it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” on the decision. President Donald Trump remarked in a Truth Social post that Nvidia made the “correct and proper decision” to reinstate Huang, adding, “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”.

The board’s independently commissioned investigation into Huang will continue, but he will regain his seat on the board. Huang is still set to testify before the Senate’s banking committee on Dec. 3, and the SEC’s investigation into Nvidia is also still set to continue.

Calling into CNBC’s Squawk Box on Monday morning, Trump reiterated that Huang’s return is good news for the country. He called Huang a “genius,” saying, “We have to protect our geniuses … The bigger threat is losing the brainpower of a person like Jensen.” In a rambling interview, Trump talked about the importance of Nvidia’s industry-leading chips.

Trump previously floated the idea of former Apple CEO Tim Cook taking over Nvidia’s top job, which gained zero traction. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been pushing for further scrutiny of Huang and Nvidia’s compliance with US export control rules. While Trump loosened the rules around how US chipmakers can do business with Chinese companies, there are still bans on selling the most advanced chips.

But we need only look to the stock market to see why the Trump administration may be changing its tune. Since the beginning of the scandal, Nvidia’s stock price has fallen dramatically, wiping out billions in market value. Monday morning’s news of Huang’s return saw premarket trading hike its share price by 30%. With Nvidia, so goes the entire stock market. And after last week’s Anthropic IPO failed to quell concerns over a growing “AI bubble” — where Nvidia is smack-dab in the center — the rebound points to investors’ confidence in Huang, Nvidia and the AI industry, spies and affairs be damned.

Within Silicon Valley, some have continually pushed for Huang’s return. Elon Musk posted an ominous “It is done” on Monday morning; Epic CEO Tim Sweeney posted a link to AC/DC’s Back in Black, a nod to Huang’s affinity for expensive black leather jackets.

In a recent development, the tech industry, perhaps more than any other, thrives on the narrative of the god-like startup founder. It’s why Jensen Huang was synonymous with Nvidia, Sam Altman with OpenAI and Dario Amodei with Anthropic. And this is not the first time a major tech CEO’s departure has caused such a commotion.

“[Huang’s] return may help restore investor confidence, but the upheaval echoes Sam Altman’s brief ouster and reinstatement at OpenAI,” Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne noted, “raising similar questions about corporate governance and the outsized influence of individual leaders over the future of AI.”.

According to recent reports, altman was fired and reinstated within a chaotic five-day period in 2023. The OpenAI board accused Altman of lying to them, but he was ultimately welcomed back and has kept a firm grip on the now-huge AI company ever since. This episode is the basis for Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming movie, Artificial, starring Andrew Garfield as Altman, coming out next month.

Those tech founders have become increasingly intertwined with government power, particularly since Trump’s return to office. Many Major Tech executives, including Huang, have donated billions in personal funds for Trump’s projects, such as his inauguration fund and prepares for a White House ballroom. It’s led many tech critics to argue that Big Tech is buying influence to avoid regulation and oversight.

“​For years, Massive Tech has used ‘national security’ as a pretext for killing pro-competition, kids’ privacy, and AI safety bills,” remarked Sacha Haworth, founder and CEO of the Tech Oversight Project. “But when their favorite CEO’s indiscretion helps a foreign rival, those concerns are thrown out the window in favor of protecting their own interests.”.

It has been revealed that most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

Recent findings suggest that newly introduced to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is at the moment rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

In a recent development, try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

In a recent development, hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a new thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s newly introduced Skills.

Recent findings suggest that certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Recent findings suggest that are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google says:.

Industry observers note that “Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google said on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

It has been revealed that google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

Recent findings suggest that for those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google announced that it would be rolling out latest settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

Charging to 100% Every Night Wears Down Your Phone’s Battery. Try This Instead

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, apple states iPhone batteries are most comfortable at temperatures between 62 and 72 degrees Fahrenheit, and charging outside that range, whether in a hot car or inside a thick case, speeds up wear.
  • It has been revealed that voltage stress at the top of the charge range, heat from fast charging and the cumulative effects of full discharge cycles all accelerate capacity loss.
  • Age is part of it, sure, but the overnight charging habit accelerates the process considerably.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple states iPhone batteries are most comfortable at temperatures between 62 and 72 degrees Fahrenheit, and charging outside that range, whether in a hot car or inside a thick case, speeds up wear. Heat is one of two things that age a phone battery faster than normal use. The other is time spent at 100%. Avoiding both takes very little effort, and the charge limit settings on iPhones, Pixels and Galaxy phones handle part of the job for you. Here’s how to charge in a way that keeps your battery healthier for longer.

It has been revealed that voltage stress at the top of the charge range, heat from fast charging and the cumulative effects of full discharge cycles all accelerate capacity loss. The damage may not appear immediately, but it’s measurable after one year and obvious after two.

Age is part of it, sure, but the overnight charging habit accelerates the process considerably. Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity faster when they spend extended time at the top of their charge range, which is precisely where an overnight charge leaves them. The fix doesn’t require a new phone or even a new charger. It requires a small adjustment to a habit most people have never thought twice about.

Keeping a lithium-ion cell pinned at 100% creates voltage stress, and the heat generated from sitting on a charger could end up meaning the difference between keeping your current phone a little longer or having to buy a new one. So once and for all, does keeping your phone plugged in really hurt the battery? Here’s what the experts suggest.

It isn’t about immediate damage but rather how fast your battery ages over time. Understanding the difference between what will and won’t break your phone is key. Here is the truth about your charging habits.

Recent findings suggest that battery health is not just about how many times you charge your phone. It is also about how it manages voltage, temperature and maintenance. Lithium-ion batteries age fastest when they are exposed to extreme levels: 0% and 100%.

In a recent development, keeping these batteries near full charge for long stretches of time puts additional voltage stress on the cathode and electrolyte. This is why many devices use “trickle charging” or temporarily pause at 100%, topping up only when needed.

Still, the biggest threat is not overcharging, but heat. When your phone is plugged in and running demanding apps, it produces heat that accelerates chemical wear inside the battery. If you are gaming, streaming or charging on a hot day, that extra warmth does far more harm than leaving the cable plugged in overnight.

The Apple battery guide describes lithium-ion batteries as “consumable components” that naturally lose capacity over time. To slow that decline, iPhones use Optimized Battery Charging, which learns your daily routine and pauses charging at about 80% until just before you typically unplug, reducing time spent at high voltage.

Apple also advises keeping devices between 0 and 35 degrees Celsius (32 and 95 degrees Fahrenheit) and removing certain cases while charging to improve heat dissipation. You can read more on the official Apple battery support page.

Samsung offers a similar feature called Battery Protect, found in the One UI battery and device care settings. When enabled, it caps charging at 85%, which helps reduce stress during long charging sessions.

Recent findings suggest that other Android makers like Google, OnePlus and Xiaomi include comparable options — often called Adaptive Charging, Optimized Charging or Battery Care — that dynamically slow power delivery or limit charge based on your habits. These systems make it safe to leave your phone plugged in for extended periods without fear of overcharging.

Even with these safeguards, some conditions can accelerate battery wear. As mentioned before, the most common culprit is high temperatures. Even for a short period of time, leaving your phone charging in direct sunlight, in a car or under a pillow can push temperatures into unsafe zones.

Industry observers note that heavy use, such as gaming or 4K video editing, while charging can also cause temperature spikes which can degrade the battery faster. And cheap, uncertified cables or adapters may deliver unstable current that stresses cells. If your battery is already several years old, it will naturally be more sensitive to this kind of strain.

Sources indicate that there is no need to overhaul your habits, but a few tweaks can help your battery age gracefully. Start by turning on the optimization tools on your phone: Optimized Battery Charging on iPhones, Battery Protect on Samsung devices and Adaptive Charging on Google Pixels. These systems learn your routine and adjust charging speed so your phone is not sitting at 100% all night.

Recent findings suggest that keep your phone cool while charging. According to Apple, phone batteries perform best between 62 and 72 degrees Fahrenheit (16 to 22 degrees Celsius). If your phone feels hot, remove its case or move it to a better ventilated or shaded spot. Avoid tossing your phone under a pillow or too close to other electronics, like your laptop. Skip wireless chargers that trap heat overnight. Use quality chargers and cables from your phone manufacturer or trusted brands. Those cheap “fast-charge” kits you find online often deliver inconsistent current, which can cause long-term challenges.

According to recent reports, finally, try not to obsess over topping off the charge. It is perfectly fine to plug in your phone during the day for short bursts. Lithium-ion batteries actually prefer frequent, shallow charges rather than deep full cycles. There is no need to keep it between 20% and 80% all the time, but just avoid extremes when possible.

In a recent development, keeping your phone plugged in overnight or on your desk all day will not destroy its battery. That is a leftover myth from a different era of tech. Modern phones are smart enough to protect themselves, and features such as Optimized Battery Charging or Battery Protect do most of the heavy lifting for you.

According to recent reports, still, no battery lasts forever. The best way to slow the inevitable is to manage heat, use quality chargers and let the software on your phone do its job. Think of it less as “babying” your battery and more as charging with intention. A few mindful habits today can keep your phone running strong for years to come.

According to recent reports, linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

Sources indicate that so too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this latest take on the OS is the epitome of that.

According to recent reports, the distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with upcoming ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

Sources indicate that the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

Sources indicate that if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

According to recent reports, pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a new workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Recent findings suggest that another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

Sources indicate that once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

Sources indicate that as I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One issue that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI update system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an patch component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

You should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my upcoming favorite free productivity suite.

Sources indicate that pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

Meta Muse booked an Airbnb without permission – and that’s not the worst of it
