    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Few, if any, forces will reshape the economy in the coming years like artificial intelligence.
    • Two very different businesses sit near the center of that build-out.
    • Industry observers note that both stocks have slumped from their highs, and Wall Street remains divided on their respective trajectories.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 23, 2026 at 4:32PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Few, if any, forces will reshape the economy in the coming years like artificial intelligence. Companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on the chips, data centers, and the models that power it.

    Two very different businesses sit near the center of that build-out. Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) designs the semiconductors that power and train most AI systems. Meanwhile, Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +4.35%) is working to become one of the key hyperscalers providing AI compute capacity, not to mention its plan to be a key pioneer in the space economy.

    Industry observers note that both stocks have slumped from their highs, and Wall Street remains divided on their respective trajectories. While the AI revolution is major enough for both of these stocks, let's take a look at which is the better buy.

    SpaceX runs three businesses. Its space segment leverages fully reusable rockets for space exploration, but it will also serve as the backbone of many of SpaceX's future ambitions.

    According to recent reports, but SpaceX's fastest-growing business, and the one with the most financial potential, is its Super Intelligence (SI) division. SI houses the social platform X, Grok intelligence, the company's data centers, and a future terafab facility.

    Recent findings suggest that spaceX appears poised to eventually join Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet as a hyperscaler, powering the AI revolution. SpaceX reported 1.7 gigawatts (GW) of computing capacity last quarter and expects to reach 2.5-3 GW by year-end.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk also noted on the company's recent earnings call that he's highly confident the company will bring an additional 10 GW of compute online in 2027 and floated a much larger figure as a possibility. Adding 10 GW of compute in 2027 would be an extraordinary achievement.

    Sources indicate that however, one could imagine that this kind of build-out will be extremely capital-intensive. SpaceX expects to spend $35 billion to $40 billion on capital expenditures in the fourth quarter alone.

    SpaceX stock is not cheap, trading around 50x Wall Street's projected adjusted earnings per share. Analysts also expect revenue to jump from about $49 billion this year to $181 billion in 2027, nearly quadrupling. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence, Wall Street consensus estimates also project adjusted negative free cash flow of roughly $162 billion in 2027.

    Meanwhile, SpaceX's longer-term ambitions, such as large-scale orbital data centers, depend on its fully reusable super-heavy-lift rocket, Starship, becoming operational and making regular trips into space.

    No manufacturer has made a more critical contribution to the AI trade than Nvidia. Its chips serve as the lifeblood of AI models. Not only are Nvidia chips viewed as the best for general-purpose computing, but Nvidia's CUDA programming platform has been used by the majority of developers for nearly two decades.

    In a recent development, CUDA can only be used with Nvidia hardware. This makes switching or developing programs on other platforms more difficult and creates a strong moat for the organization.

    According to recent reports, nvidia also continues to put up stellar results. Last quarter's revenue more than doubled to $115.8 billion, while the company's gross margin held near 75%. Management also guided for 90% annual revenue growth to $130 billion in the current quarter, topping analyst estimates.

    However, the stock has been incredibly volatile since the scandal surrounding Jensen Huang came to light. Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following reports of multiple alleged extramarital affairs, including one reportedly with a woman who may have been a Chinese spy and who allegedly set up a network that illegally diverted Nvidia chips to China.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Industry observers note that on Nov. 23, Nvidia's board of directors surprisingly reinstated Huang as CEO. A substantial question that remains is how much of Nvidia's prior revenue, if any, may have been illegally diverted to China. What could this mean for future revenue projections if regulators crack down on such sales, as they already have begun to do?

    Lawmakers have opened investigations, and Nvidia intends to finish its own independent investigation regarding whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

    Sources indicate that while Huang's reinstatement triggered a furious rebound in Nvidia stock, it's still down 12% this year. There are still risks, depending on what upcoming information comes to light or what investigations find.

    Sources indicate that but Nvidia still makes an industry-leading product in high demand among customers in the hottest industry on the planet right now. Even after the recent rally, the stock still trades at slightly over 10 times its projected adjusted fiscal 2028 sales.

    Recent findings suggest that while both SpaceX and Nvidia carry risks, and I wouldn't necessarily get overly aggressive on either, Nvidia is the better buy right now due to a valuation that has likely priced in a significant portion of the risk. SpaceX has tremendous potential, but I suspect it will struggle to balance growth with the need to continue raising significant capital.

    Tech Report: Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (897 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
    • With Claude Ship, confirmed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said.
    • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A latest feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

    With Claude Ship, confirmed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

    Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

    “Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic stated. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

    Sources indicate that the new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise intends. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic remarked, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

    Sources indicate that PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

    Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

    As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic stated.

    “It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic said it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

    Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

    But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

    In a recent development, “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

    ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

    Also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

    Industry observers note that “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he noted. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

    Ultimately, Gewirtz remarked he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

    “Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the company and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he said.

    Developer platforms overall are adapting to the newly introduced state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

    Sources indicate that individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “users won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

    Still, that depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the newly introduced PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

    According to recent reports, anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

    Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

    As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Phone-maker Nothing Technology is breaking away from its typical retro-inspired designs with a upcoming pair of AI-powered earbuds, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.
    • Industry observers note that the Ear Note earbuds are designed primarily to maximize the recording functionality.
    • Sources indicate that the earbuds can capture and transcribe phone calls, while the charging case has its own microphone to record in-person conversations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Phone-maker Nothing Technology is breaking away from its typical retro-inspired designs with a upcoming pair of AI-powered earbuds, as reported earlier by Bloomberg. The company confirmed via an X post that its Ear Note wireless earbuds will be available starting Dec. 8.

    Industry observers note that the Ear Note earbuds are designed primarily to maximize the recording functionality. While other AI earbuds have already hit the market, the Ear Note is the first to record both phone calls and in-person conversations.

    Sources indicate that the earbuds can capture and transcribe phone calls, while the charging case has its own microphone to record in-person conversations. To mitigate privacy concerns, the case only records with a physical button press — a tell that could reveal when audio is being captured around the Ear Note user.

    Nothing shared that the Ear Note will work with multiple popular AI agents, but the full list of compatible software has not yet been released. The Ear Note works in tandem with an app that stores recordings from the earbuds and case, creating transcriptions and summaries similar to those created by the popular Otter AI app.

    The Nothing brand has developed a cult following for combining lifestyle and fashion trends in its suite of smartphones, headphones, speakers and watches.

    The full product lineup is built with modern hardware, but mimics warm, nearly retrofuturist design sensibilities. The blocky Ear Note charging case continues this trend while taking the manufacturer’s tech in a new direction.

    In the lead-up to the Ear Note’s reveal, Nothing CEO Carl Pei described the earbuds in an X post as “a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product.”.

    In a Bloomberg interview, Pei indicated that Nothing isn’t trying to create AI agents or software, but that the organization has a “really interesting opportunity to be the hardware layer to AI.”.

    Sources indicate that it’s at the moment unclear how much the Ear Note earbuds and case will cost when they’re released next month. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the company hasn’t settled on a price just yet. The most expensive earbuds currently available on the Nothing store cost $149.

    It has been revealed that whether you’re covering your eyes, plugging your ears or slapping a timepiece on your wrist, there’s now an ever-present option to record the world around you. Multiple companies have created their own versions of smart glasses, earbuds and watches with augmented reality capabilities.

    Industry observers note that now that AI is the flavor du jour, these existing features are being enhanced by new ways to scan and interact with the surrounding environment. That means a lot of visual and auditory data is being recorded by wearable devices, and very rarely with the consent of all parties involved.

    The most immediate risk factors are associated with video recording – public distrust of smart glasses is so widespread that they’ve colloquially been coined “pervert glasses,” as folks fear they fundamentally break an unspoken social contract by obscuring public recording from other people.

    But audio recording, enabled by Apple’s latest smartwatches, the Amazon Bee, Plaud earbuds and the fresh Ear Note, is also raising concerns, not least because many states require all-party consent before you can record conversations.

    The Ear Note’s ability to record every bit of audio, from phone calls to in-person conversations, means it will be handling more sensitive information than other AI-powered earbuds. The company will need to face new challenges to ensure security measures are in place to prevent private chats from leaking.

    It has been revealed that at the very least, it seems as though Nothing Technology is aware of these privacy risks. According to Bloomberg, the firm created a data and security team to address concerns that cropped up during the Ear Note’s development. The company has also “obtained the same privacy certifications as competing recording products and worked with law firms to assess potential risks and safeguards.”.

    Pei called wearables with recording functionality a sensitive space, and noted the design team was “extra careful to not take any risks.” The Ear Note earbuds and case are largely controlled by user commands, including tactile button presses that begin the recording process.

    SpaceX Sued by 2 States Over Grok’s Sexualized Images of Women and Children

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s firm violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.
    • Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX.
    • In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s firm violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

    Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

    In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

    Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down.

    Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

    Industry observers note that “When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones stated. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this firm accountable.”.

    Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

    “It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”.

    Sources indicate that grok Imagine launched on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

    Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

    “It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield mentioned in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”.

    During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

    Sources indicate that in a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX noted that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The company said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

    Industry observers note that in July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The tech giant seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

    SpaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing consumers to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

    Monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Substantial Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the firm intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

    Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (538 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
    • After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
    • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a new Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber says that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

    After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

    According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

    While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

    Sources indicate that starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

    Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

    Uber says the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

    “Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

    Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

    “Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

    Uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

    Sources indicate that uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.
